findings.title: Moon (Predicted Ephemeris)
findings.subtitle: Predicted Moon · 0.003 AU · Alt +24.1° · Above Horizon

evidence.verificationMethod: Predicted for the given time and place; not measured in the image
limitations: Predicted with Meeus (1998) chapter 47 in full, as ERFA's eraMoon98, for the Moon and ERFA eraEpv00 for the Earth, with light time, for the recorded capture time, its time zone taken from the GPS position and agreeing with the GPS time stamp, and place; not measured in the recording.
Seen from the given place at sea level (topocentric): its parallax is applied, and its right ascension and declination are astrometric (light time only).
Its altitude and azimuth are apparent and airless: refraction at 1010 hPa and 10 degrees C (Saemundsson 1986) would lift it to +24.09 degrees, and the real air differs most near the horizon.

Its uncertainty, 38.0 arcsec, adds the method's documented worst error (18.4 arcsec here), 0.00 for light deflection applied as for a star, 13.8 for UT1 - UTC taken as 0 (within 0.9 s), 4.8 for a place up to 9 km above sea level, 1 for polar motion, and 0.0 for the time scale.
The moment is UTC; TT comes from ERFA's leap-second table, and UT1 is taken as UTC, within 0.9 s.

findings.title: Sirius
findings.subtitle: Predicted Star (CMa) · Alpha Canis Majoris · 9 CMa · HR 2491 · HIP 32349 · 2.6 pc · Alt +75.5° Az 309.3° · Above Horizon

evidence.verificationMethod: Predicted for the given time and place; not measured in the image
evidence.distanceUncertaintyNote: Distance interval [2.6, 2.6] pc: 1000/parallax from Hipparcos 2007, with the interval from the parallax error
limitations: Predicted from its Hipparcos 2007 catalog row (epoch J2016.0), moved by its proper motion to the date, for the recorded capture time, its time zone taken from the GPS position and agreeing with the GPS time stamp, and place; not measured in the recording.
Its brightness is the catalog's own Hipparcos Hp magnitude, not the usual V.

Placed in the sky for that moment and place, at sea level; near the horizon it sits a little low, since the air's bending of light is left out. Its stated uncertainty adds UT1 - UTC (up to 13.5 arcseconds), polar motion, its own parallax (left out of its place), the stored precision of its motion, and, for a row with no proper motion or radial velocity, the motion it may have, up to the fastest star in the tiles; the catalog's own position and motion errors are not in it.

warnings: The file names no time zone for its capture time: it was taken from the time zone at the photo's GPS position, which agrees with its GPS time stamp.
